correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the crown order and fence lift explicitly. Every lift step changes by at most one, so a self-map has winding in {-1,0,1}. Equality forces every step to have the same sign, giving exactly the level-preserving dihedral automorphisms. At winding zero, a closed walk of length 2n cannot visit all 2n residues without total variation at least 4n-2, so the image omits a crown point and lies in a beat-reducible fence; hence the map is null-homotopic. Minimal-space rigidity separates distinct automorphisms. The bundled verifier independently enumerates n=2,3,4,5 and directly checks components for n=2,3,4.

value.rationale: Crowns are canonical finite weak models of the circle and occur independently in finite topology and order theory. The theorem gives a complete self-homotopy classification for the entire family, showing exactly how finite-space homotopy is more rigid than ordinary circle homotopy: all zero-winding endomorphisms collapse to one class, while every nonzero class is forced to be an actual automorphism. This is a natural structural invariant rather than an arbitrary finite census.
